summary: Modified the dev server runner in scripts/dev-server.ts to spawn the agent as a `tsx watch` child instead of importing it in-process, enabling automatic restarts on agent-server source edits. The runner still waits for the agent's WebSocket port to accept connections before starting Vite, and stops both processes if either dies. Verified by editing apps/agent-server/src/server.ts multiple times and observing restarts plus automatic browser reconnection.
decisions: Run the agent as a `tsx watch` child process rather than importing it in-process, so edits under apps/agent-server restart the agent without a manual restart command.

Set the agent child's stdin to 'ignore' because `tsx watch` silently fails to boot when its stdin is a piped stream that nothing writes to (discovered by isolating the failure with manual spawn tests).
Keep Vite waiting on the agent's WebSocket port before starting, preserving the 'connect after agent is ready' startup ordering.
If either the agent or Vite process exits, stop the other as well (linked lifecycle in the runner).
errors: Initial `tsx watch` startup timed out and the agent never reported 'server listening' when spawned from the runner; root cause turned out to be a piped stdin causing `tsx watch` to never execute the program, fixed by setting stdio to ['ignore', logDescriptor, logDescriptor].
An ad-hoc `tsc --noEmit` invocation produced false-positive errors about 'node:net' not being typed because @types/node wasn't picked up; treated as noise rather than a real issue.
